blocks.html: A container is a lightweight and standalone package of an application with all its dependencies like libraries, frameworks and runtime.

blocks.html: Containerisation is considered as the lightweight version of the virtualisation.

blocks.html: Containers are lightweight and require less hardware resources than virtual machines.

blocks.html: Each container runs as a native process of the host OS they are much faster to start.
blocks.text: Each container runs as a native process of the host OS they are much faster to start.

blocks.html: Because the isolation of containers relies on OS level primitives, therefore the containers are exposed to wider level of security vulnerabilites.

blocks.html: Its possible to run containers inside the virtual machines.
blocks.text: Its possible to run containers inside the virtual machines.

blocks.html: To reduce the security vulnerability by reducing the attack surface, containers are sometimes run into virtual machines. Deciding whether to run containers directly on the container engine on host OS or on virtual machines is basically a tradeoff between (flexibility+maintenecne) and security.
